new: Find similar on the Search page, and GET /{ds}/search/similar for GraphRAG: the nearest resources to a text, a vector or a resource, with their descriptions.
Full-text queries written for Stardog, Virtuoso, QLever, GraphDB's connectors and Jena's LARQ run unchanged.
Map page: show or hide each layer, choose the base map, zoom to all the data and go fullscreen.
Describe pages with tabs: overview, all properties, incoming links, graph, data model and RDF.
A Share button that copies a link to the view you are on, and a copy button next to every IRI.
improved: Transitive property paths and nearest-vector ORDER BY queries are many times faster.
Every page uses the full width of the window.
fixed: Spatial filters over a geometry reached by a property path with an alternative or a repeat, and GeoSPARQL relations inside EXISTS, give the right answers.

new: The project is now called TripleTrail: the binary, packages, image, namespaces (tt:, tts:, ttsh:, ttfx:, ttfn:) and settings (TRIPLETRAIL_*) carry the new name.

Fuseki parity: full-text search with jena-text's text:query and your own indexed properties, the SHACL and RDF Patch services, compaction and Fuseki's admin endpoints; tripletrail config import-fuseki translates a Fuseki configuration.
Maps and APIs: OGC API Features and vector tiles, a map page, a REST API and GraphQL generated from your shapes.
Describe pages, the Workbench and a search builder in the web UI, laid out by your SHACL shapes.
Facade-X and RML: query CSV, JSON, XML and spreadsheets as RDF, and run RML mappings.
Access control: users, groups and per-graph rights, with Basic auth, OpenID Connect sign-in and an audit log.
RDFS and OWL RL entailment into a graph kept up to date with every write, and SHACL rules.
improved: Faster queries, writes and loads across the board; full-text queries written for Blazegraph and Stardog run unchanged.

new: tripletrail serve replaces Fuseki: the SPARQL 1.1 Protocol and the Graph Store Protocol on Fuseki's URLs, and Fuseki's admin API under /$/ (datasets, backups, tasks, statistics, server).
A web UI: manage datasets and query them with MatGUI, with a table, map, chart and graph view. MatGUI is built in, so it works without internet access.
Read-only datasets: attach a published release memory-mapped, so it opens at once and shares memory with the page cache.
Aliases: point a stable name at a dataset version, swap it to a new release without downtime and roll back the same way.
Snapshots to a new dataset directory, backups to compressed N-Quads, and restore from a backup.
Explain shows TripleTrail's plan with row counts and timings, and where the spatial and range indexes were used.
A Docker image (ghcr.io/matdata-eu/tripletrail) with a health check, /$/ready for load balancers, graceful shutdown and a JSON request log.
A short tour, About and this list of what is new in each release.
improved: FILTERs on a numeric range, such as a kilometre post between two values, are answered from a value-ordered index instead of a scan.
